newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND'S VALIO EYES BALTIC EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND'S VALIO EYES BALTIC EXPANSION.

text.p: Finnish food group Valio on Monday said that it was looking at ways to expand its operations in the Baltic states, which may involve starting a production plant for ice cream and cheese in Estonia, Latvia or Lithuania.
Valio, a privately-owned company, already has a plant in the southern Estonian town of Tartu making yoghurts for the Estonian market and for Latvia and Lithuania.
"We have been contemplating making ice cream and/or cheese," Valio vice-president Jaako Lehtonen told Reuters in an interview at a Baltics investment conference here.
He said that no firm decision had been made yet but that talks had been held with various companies in the Baltics.
He said the new project may involve starting a manufacturing plant or taking a stake in an existing company.
Lehtonen said that Valio had around 38 percent of the yoghurt market in Estonia and smaller shares in Latvia and Lithuania.
He added that sales of Valio products in Estonia were around 200 million kroons and some three million dollars in Latvia and Lithuania.
Lehtonen said that Valio now owned 92 percent of the Tartu plant, which makes products under the Alma brand.
